children: HSBC has abandoned its long-standing “on hold” forecast and now looks for the Federal Reserve to deliver a 25-basis-point rate increase at Wednesday’s FOMC meeting.
The bank then expects one further quarter-point hike before year-end 2026, after which policy would stay unchanged through 2027.

The implied tightening path is unusually shallow. Most hiking cycles since the 1990s have totaled at least 200 basis points; the 1997 episode, limited to a single 25-basis-point move, is the closest modern analogue.

) often slips in the early phase of a tightening cycle before gradually recouping those losses. HSBC is nevertheless holding its year-end S&P 500 target at 8,100. The firm’s economists argue that both consumers and corporations remain sufficiently resilient to absorb modestly higher borrowing costs without a material slowdown in spending or investment.

The combination of a limited rate adjustment and continued private-sector strength underpins the bank’s view that equities can still reach the targeted level even as the Fed edges policy slightly tighter.

title: HSBC calls for the shallowest hiking cycle since 1997
